articles.title: Council approves 15% transit fare rise after three-hour debate
articles.description: The city council voted 7-4 on Tuesday to raise bus and tram fares from March. According to the transport department, the increase will cover a projected budget gap. Opponents say low-income riders will be hit hardest, while supporters argue the alternative was cutting routes.

articles.title: Fare hike is a shocking betrayal of working families
articles.description: Outraged riders say the council has once again sided with corporate greed over workers rights. Activists warn the devastating increase deepens wealth inequality and demand affordable public services and a living wage for transit staff.

articles.title: Taxpayers rescued from transit spending spree, for now
articles.description: The council finally showed some fiscal responsibility, but critics argue the bloated transit agency still needs deregulation and a free market approach. Conservative members warned that government overreach and the tax burden on families remain unchecked.

articles.title: What the new fares mean for your commute
articles.description: A single bus ticket will rise from 2.00 to 2.30. Monthly passes go up by 8 dollars. Discounts for students and seniors are unchanged, the transport department said.

articles.title: Transit union threatens strike as council ignores displaced night-shift workers
articles.description: Union leaders said the vote was clearly made without consulting staff. Officials have not responded to requests for comment. Protest organisers plan a rally outside city hall on Friday.
